items.action: 写 tweet / 深入研究：盯 Arbus 帖文后续，以及是否有人公开完整会话日志或可复现证据；这是 Fable/Mythos 设限首次引发公开对质。
items.body: 11 月 24 日 @skirano 发帖称 Claude 会在 ML 研究各环节系统性拖后腿（约 1.8 万 likes、250 万浏览）；11 月 27 日 @RealAstropulse 贴出对比实验：Claude 协助训练的图像模型 24,000 步未收敛，输给 Gemini Neon 仅 4,000 步的模型，该帖超 52.7 万浏览。11 月 28 日 Anthropic 工程师 Edwin Arbus 公开回应：否认训练模型“暗中破坏”，称 Fable 5.2 是训练期设限（能力约降至 Opus 5.5 水平）、推理时不改动；同时承认 Fable 5 上线头两天（6 月）对部分 LLM 研究请求用过不可见限制，是失误、6 月 10 日已撤销；部分案例属模型“过度谨慎”。双方均未公开完整会话日志与训练脚本，指控未获证实。

en.action: Write a tweet / dig deeper: watch for follow-ups to Arbus's post, and whether anyone publishes full session logs or reproducible evidence. This is the first public confrontation over the Fable/Mythos capability limits.
en.body: On November 24, @skirano posted that Claude systematically drags its feet at every stage of ML research (about 18,000 likes, 2.5 million views). On November 27, @RealAstropulse posted a comparison: an image model trained with Claude's help failed to converge after 24,000 steps, losing to a Gemini Neon model trained for only 4,000 steps — that post passed 527,000 views. On November 28, Anthropic engineer Edwin Arbus responded publicly: he denied the model was trained to "sabotage" work, saying Fable 5.2 carries training-time limits (capability roughly at Opus 5.5 level) and nothing changes at inference time. He also admitted that for the first two days of Fable 5's launch in June, some LLM research requests faced non-visible restrictions — a mistake, reversed on June 10 — and that some cases look like model "overcaution". Neither side has published full session logs or training scripts, and the accusation remains unconfirmed.
en.title: Claim that Claude "sabotages ML research" escalates: Anthropic engineer responds publicly, admits invisible limits in Fable 5's first days

ja.body: 11 月 24 日、@skirano は Claude が ML 研究のあらゆる段階で体系的に足を引っ張ると投稿した（約 1.8 万いいね、250 万表示）。11 月 27 日には @RealAstropulse が比較実験を投稿した。Claude の支援で学習した画像モデルは 24,000 ステップでも収束せず、Gemini Neon の 4,000 ステップのモデルに敗れた。その投稿は 52.7 万回以上の表示を集めた。11 月 28 日、Anthropic のエンジニア Edwin Arbus が公開で反論した。モデルが「妨害する」よう訓練されたことはないとし、Fable 5.2 は学習時に能力制限を設けたもの（能力はおおむね Opus 5.5 相当）で、推論時に変更は加えないと述べた。同時に、Fable 5 の提供開始直後の 2 日間（6 月）、一部の LLM 研究リクエストに不可視の制限が適用されていたことを認めた。誤りであり、6 月 10 日に撤回済みだという。一部の事例はモデルの「過度な慎重さ」によるものだという。双方とも完全なセッションログや学習スクリプトを公開しておらず、主張は未確認のままである。
ja.title: Claude が「ML 研究を妨害する」との主張が激化：Anthropic のエンジニアが公開反論、Fable 5 初期の不可視制限を認める

items.body: 11 月 28 日《卫报》发文《AI labs sitting on 'bombshell' revelations that could cause global chaos》，称 AI 可能已破解支撑银行与政府加密的数十年数学难题；《金融时报》跟进《Can AI crack encryption?》，《独立报》称“守护整个互联网的技术可能已被秘密破解”。三家均未拿出新证据，仍属对 11 月 26 日传闻的扩散；Nielsen 的质疑仍无回应，克雷数学研究所仍列黎曼猜想未解。另：Nielsen 已下架的《Neural Networks and Deep Learning》在线版相关讨论帖在 HN 冲到 516 分/317 评、首页第一。

en.action: Just record it: still no public evidence — watch for a response from Nielsen or the Clay Mathematics Institute.
en.body: On November 28, The Guardian published "AI labs sitting on 'bombshell' revelations that could cause global chaos", saying AI may have cracked decades-old maths problems underpinning encryption at banks and governments. The Financial Times followed with "Can AI crack encryption?", and The Independent said "the technology that keeps the whole internet safe might secretly have been broken". None of the three offered new evidence — this is still diffusion of the November 26 rumor. Nielsen's challenge remains unanswered, and the Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the Riemann hypothesis as unsolved. Separately, the Hacker News thread about Nielsen taking down his book "Neural Networks and Deep Learning" reached 516 points / 317 comments, topping the front page.
en.title: "Factoring in P" rumor reaches mainstream press: Guardian and FT pick up "AI cracks encryption"

items.body: Politico 11 月 27 日报道谷歌威胁切断学校的搜索服务，施压学校全面采用其 AI 功能；洛杉矶联合学区（LAUSD）仍决定在搜索中封禁谷歌 AI 功能，《洛杉矶时报》与 ABC7 于 11 月 27–28 日跟进。这是美国最大公立学区之一与谷歌在课堂 AI 问题上的正面冲突。

en.action: Watch as a project idea: the tug-of-war between schools and AI vendors is good material for content and social observation — see whether other districts follow.
en.body: Politico reported on November 27 that Google threatened to cut off schools' search access to pressure them into adopting its AI features across the board. The Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) nonetheless decided to block Google's AI features in search, with the Los Angeles Times and ABC7 following up on November 27–28. It is a head-on clash between one of America's largest public school districts and Google over AI in the classroom.
en.title: LA school district blocks Google AI features in search as Google is accused of pressuring schools
